summary:
# SmartCrop AI – Intelligent Farming Assistant

SmartCrop AI is a simple, user-friendly application designed to help farmers make smarter and more sustainable farming decisions.

Farmers can create a profile for their farm by entering its name, selecting its location on an interactive map, and recording its latitude and longitude. They can also enter important information such as soil type, soil moisture, current crops, available water, and farm size.

The application combines this information with NASA Earth observation data, including rainfall, temperature, and soil moisture information. An AI assistant analyzes the farm's conditions and the farmer's needs to suggest suitable crop rotation plans, improve soil health, and help save water.

The app can also compare different farming strategies and provide easy-to-understand recommendations.

Our goal is to build an accessible application that anyone can use, even without technical experience. Smart Crop AI brings maps, NASA data, and artificial intelligence together to support smarter farming, healthier soil, and more climate-resilient agriculture.
details:
Smart Crop: Climate-Smart Farm Planning

What it does: SmartCrop helps farmers explore crop and water planning using their farm’s location, boundaries, soil information, and climate conditions. Farmers can mark a field on a map or enter coordinates, view satellite imagery, use GPS, and see boundary lengths and estimated area in units such as dunams, square meters, hectares, or square feet. The map also checks OpenStreetMap features and excludes mapped buildings and water areas from the estimated farmland area.

The app presents climate information, soil-health indicators, crop-rotation suggestions, water guidance, and farm reports. It uses NASA POWER climate observations. Some vegetation values and recommendations are illustrative because this is a prototype.

Benefits and intended impact: SmartCrop aims to make farm planning easier and more locally relevant. By bringing climate, soil, and field information together, it can help farmers compare crop rotations, use water more thoughtfully, and consider practices that support soil health. The broader goal is to support climate-resilient agriculture and contribute to more sustainable food production.

Tools and technology: The project includes an Android app built with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Room, Hilt, and Gradle, as well as an HTML, CSS, and JavaScript browser version. The web map uses Leaflet, OpenStreetMap data and search, and Esri satellite imagery. The project was developed in Android Studio and can use a GPS-enabled phone or browser; it does not require specialized farm hardware.

What makes it creative: SmartCrop combines field mapping with climate monitoring, soil-health scoring, and crop-rotation planning in one tool. It also supports both Arabic and English and offers familiar local area units such as the dunam.

Factors considered: The team considered ease of use, language, GPS and map access, area-unit conversion, water and building exclusions, and the effect of limited or incomplete map data. Recommendations are intended as planning support; farmers should confirm field conditions and consult agricultural experts for decisions with significant consequences.
